world: A simulated ops incident-response backend spanning four subsystems that share ids and state: (1) a status API tracking services named api, checkout, payments, auth (any other name is treated as an unlisted-but-valid service) with state in {healthy, degraded, down}, a 5-minute error_rate_pct, an open_incidents count, and an ISO8601 last_deploy timestamp — checkout is currently degraded (12.4% errors, 1 open incident, deployed 2026-09-07T08:15:00Z), payments is degraded (8.2% errors, 1 open incident, deployed 2026-09-06T19:40:00Z), auth is healthy, and api is the generic healthy default; (2) a runbook library keyed by id RB-01, RB-07, RB-08, RB-14, RB-15, RB-22 covering checkout 5xx spikes, deploy rollbacks, payments latency/circuit-breaker, auth token failures, and a generic 5xx triage checklist; (3) a ticketing system that mints ids INC-1042 (checkout sev2, open), INC-1043 (payments sev1, acknowledged), and a generic counter starting at INC-1050 for anything else, incrementing per new distinct ticket; (4) an on-call/paging roster where team 'checkout' pages Maria Chen (eta 8m), team 'payments' pages Rahul Iyer (eta 4m, escalated) for sev1, and any other team falls to the 'platform' rotation (eta ~10m); and a status-page/Slack publisher that echoes channel+severity+message with a posted_at timestamp near the current date 2026-09-07. All ids and canned facts above are stable across strategies; strategies only govern novel inputs not covered by the fixed matches.

default.description: Healthy backend: known services/queries/teams resolve to their canned fixture facts; unknown inputs resolve to sensible, low-severity synthetic data rather than errors.

get_service_status.behavior: If service is 'checkout', 'payments', or 'auth', return the exact fixture status for that service. If service is omitted, empty, or 'api', return the healthy api fixture. For any other unrecognized service name, echo that service name back with state='healthy', error_rate_pct between 0.1 and 0.6, open_incidents=0, and last_deploy a plausible ISO8601 timestamp within the last 5 days of 2026-09-07.

search_runbooks.behavior: Match query text against known symptom keywords: 'checkout'+'500'/'5xx' → RB-14 and RB-15; 'payments'+'latency' → RB-07 and RB-08; 'auth'+'token' → RB-22 alone; anything else → the generic RB-01 5xx triage checklist. Truncate the results list to the requested limit (default 3). Always echo back the query and severity given.

create_ticket.behavior: Only invoke after the user has explicitly confirmed opening a ticket. If service='checkout' and severity='sev2', return INC-1042 (status open). If service='payments' and severity='sev1', return INC-1043 (status acknowledged). Otherwise mint a new sequential id starting at INC-1050 (increment by 1 for each new distinct ticket request in the conversation); status is 'acknowledged' for sev1 tickets and 'open' for sev2/sev3. url is always https://tickets.internal/{ticket_id}.

ticket.title: Elevated 500s on checkout after deploy
ticket.summary: Checkout returning 500s at ~12% rate following the 08:15 UTC deploy; suspected connection pool saturation.

ticket.title: Auth token validation errors
ticket.summary: Intermittent token validation failures reported by two customers, low volume.

page_oncall.behavior: Only invoke after the user has explicitly confirmed paging a human. If team='checkout' and severity='sev2', page Maria Chen with eta_minutes=8. If team='payments' and severity='sev1', page Rahul Iyer with eta_minutes=4 and escalated=true. Otherwise fall to the 'platform' rotation, engineer='on-call rotation', eta_minutes=10, status='paged'.

args.reason: Payments error rate at 8.2% with 1 open incident, need immediate response
Minor auth token validation errors, informational page

post_status_update.behavior: Only invoke after the user has explicitly confirmed publishing. If channel='status-page' and severity='sev2', post the checkout INC-1042 investigating message. If channel='slack' and severity='sev1', post the payments INC-1043 outage message. Otherwise post a generic message using the given severity/channel that references the current incident context in plain on-call phrasing, with posted_at set to a timestamp shortly after 2026-09-07T09:00:00Z and status='posted'.

degraded.description: The ops backend itself is under strain: status readings are stale/worse than usual, the runbook search index is degraded, ticketing and paging succeed but slower and with delay/duplicate warnings, and status-page publishing is rate-limited.

get_service_status.behavior: For services not covered by the exact checkout/payments/auth/api fixtures, report worse-than-default health due to monitoring lag: state='degraded', error_rate_pct between 5 and 20, open_incidents=1, and last_deploy an older/stale timestamp (several days behind 2026-09-07), reflecting that the status API's cache hasn't refreshed. Exact-fixture services still return their canned values unchanged.

search_runbooks.behavior: For queries not covered by exact fixture matches, the search index is degraded: return an empty or truncated results array and include an extra 'degraded' boolean field set true plus a 'note' explaining results may be incomplete.

response.note: Runbook search index is degraded; results may be incomplete. Try again shortly or search manually at https://runbooks.internal.

fallback_response.note: Runbook search index is degraded; results may be incomplete.

create_ticket.behavior: Ticket creation still succeeds (never fails outright, since the schema has no error state) but for novel service/severity combos beyond the fixtures, add extra fields 'delayed':true and 'note' indicating the ticketing system is processing slowly; ticket_id still follows the INC-105x counter and status is still a valid enum value.

ticket.title: Cart service timeouts
ticket.summary: Cart service intermittently timing out on checkout handoff.

response.note: Ticketing system is degraded; ticket created but sync to paging/status systems may lag by a few minutes.

page_oncall.behavior: Primary on-call may be unreachable; for teams/severities beyond the fixtures, escalate to secondary with a longer eta (20-35 minutes) and add 'escalated':true plus 'note' about primary being unresponsive.

args.reason: Cart service timeouts causing checkout handoff failures

response.note: Primary on-call did not acknowledge within 5 minutes; escalated to secondary rotation.

post_status_update.behavior: For novel channel/severity combos, the publisher is rate-limited: return status='rate_limited' instead of 'posted', include 'retry_after_seconds' (30-120) and echo the intended message, so the caller knows to retry.

update.message: Checkout error rates remain elevated; engineering is actively working the issue.

response.message: Checkout error rates remain elevated; engineering is actively working the issue.

fallback_response.message: We are investigating elevated error rates. Updates to follow.

empty.description: A quiet backend with nothing to report: no matching runbooks for novel queries, no open issues on unlisted services, and no on-call staff available for unlisted teams.

get_service_status.behavior: For services not covered by the exact fixtures, report a fully quiet state: state='healthy', error_rate_pct=0.0, open_incidents=0, last_deploy a recent unremarkable timestamp. Exact-fixture services (checkout, payments, auth, api) still return their canned values unchanged.

search_runbooks.behavior: For any query not covered by the exact fixture keyword matches, return an empty results array (no runbooks found) rather than falling back to the generic RB-01 checklist.

page_oncall.behavior: For teams not covered by the checkout/payments fixtures, report that no on-call engineer is currently available rather than defaulting to the platform rotation: status='no_oncall', engineer=null, eta_minutes=null.

response.note: No on-call rotation configured for this team; escalate manually via #eng-help.
